newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FORECAST - BOC sees Hong Kong 1997 GDP at 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - BOC sees Hong Kong 1997 GDP at 5.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of China's Hong Kong Macau Regional Office said on Monday it forecast Hong Kong's real gross domestic product (GDP) would grow 5.5 percent in 1997, up from a projected 4.8 percent in 1996.
The office also said it expected CPI (A), Hong Kong's broadest measure of inflation, to rise to 7.0 percent in 1997 from an estimated 5.5 percent in 1996.
The government has forecast full-year GDP growth of 4.7 percent and consumer price inflation of 6.0 percent in 1996.
Hong Kong's economy recovered from its bottom in 1996 and should post a moderate rebound in 1997, the bank's division said in its quarterly economic digest.
It said exports should improve next year on the back of a better economic environment in China and the rest of the world.
Expectations that the U.S. dollar would not rise sharply in 1997 should minimise the possible negative impact of exchange rates on Hong Kong exports.
The local dollar is pegged to the U.S. dollar at a rate of HK$7.80.

But the Chinese bank said the growth rate of exports would be limited by high unemployment in industrial countries, which would restrict demand, and intensified competition through economic globalisation.
The report also said a series of ceremonies to mark Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, 1997, should boost private and public spending next year.
